rationale: G2r5.1 is ADDRESSED. The new F2 predicate no longer treats unrelated panels' round numbers as chronology: every visible outside-tip registration refuses at acceptance and read-back. AC-11 explicitly covers the old-round-5/new-round-1 counterexample, a genuine matching audit, and counter-only changes. Real-git predicate probes using the actual panel writer/scanner, SHA gate, ancestry helper and net-effect helper confirm that normal completion descendants and the #239 topology satisfy the new rule, while a later unlanded registration refuses regardless of its local counter or abandonment. The specification now accurately separates git facts from forgeable panel files and audit metadata, and explicitly prices the additional fallback acceptance reach rather than claiming authentication. The override contract retains fresh claim-time authorization, complete failure-set coverage and fail-closed indeterminate reads. No remaining spec-gate blocker was established through the G2 trust-boundary lens. This approves the specification at 8b3a5535, not an implementation of its proposed features.

findings.title: Round-5 ask status
findings.detail: G2r5.1 — ADDRESSED. spec.md:414-425 removes anchors and all round comparisons, and refuses on any visible registration with a well-formed reviewed SHA outside the tip's history. Rounds have no acceptance authority, including between separate slugs. spec.md:445-448 requires F2 again on automatic read-back even with a valid matching audit. AC-11(x-c), lines 863-867, reproduces the genuinely later independent default-round-1 panel behind an old round-5 panel, covers fresh reattest and read-back with a previously genuine matching tuple, and pins that changing only the counter cannot change the refusal. AC-11(i-a) retains the positive in-place rebased-round case by explicitly overwriting the old registration; no cross-directory chronological exception remains. AC-18 pins the corresponding ADR-0041 amendment. None of my round-5 required changes is PARTIAL or MISSED. The scratch predicate probe also confirms refusal with later counters 1, 6 and 0. Evidence: round6-probe.json and repo/internal/lifecycle/g2_round6_probe_test.go in this scratch directory.

findings.title: Normal completion descendants and #239 remain recoverable
findings.detail: F2 checks reviewed SHA ancestry of the current spec tip, rather than equality with the second parent. Therefore a normal one-round review at B followed by complete-authored descendant D passes; additional fix commits also pass when the final registration names a landed ancestor. The real-git probe creates a genuinely different completion tree after review, lands it, then carries the spec through a sibling PR into main and fast-forwards the spec. Its landing is absent from FirstParentMerges, exactly one source-named two-parent fallback merge is reachable, ContentSubsumedOutcome reports SubsumptionLanded, and F2 passes before and after this #239 transformation. Co-bumping the same panel to another landed descendant also passes. The surviving bead branch is deleted, matching the fallback recovery case. A separate old registration at a rebased-away SHA can conservatively refuse a legitimate landing under the skill's documented per-round-slug pattern; R4.2 explicitly states that limit and offers the dependent's scoped override. It is not a hidden normal-path dead end or an unsound chronology exception. These are predicate/primitive probes: the proposed fallback reattest and read-back are not implemented at the reviewed commit.

findings.title: Forgeability and the new fallback reach are now stated accurately
findings.detail: A bd metadata writer can fabricate a shape-valid audit and binding in one update; actor, op, timestamp and SHA shape do not authenticate an operator. Tuple equality prevents accidental reuse of a genuine audit after a different binding is written, while re-running F1/F3/F4 preserves scan-derived candidate count, surviving-tip and current-tip content constraints. F2 is a filesystem assertion, not a git fact. The probe confirms that an abandoned outside-tip registration still refuses, and that rewriting its SHA to a landed SHA or deleting its directory removes that refusal. spec.md:452-456 explicitly documents this panel-edit residual and the resulting NEW undirected off-first-parent acceptance reach; AC-11(ix-g) and AC-18 pin it. An author of git history can also forge a source-naming merge subject; a subject is nomination, not proof of the operator's intent or merge destination. Those limits fit ADR-0037 section 8 and the declared non-goal of authenticating agent-writable state. They do not justify claiming that a JSONL audit proves an operator ran reattest. The revised text makes that distinction.

findings.title: Selection and override authority remain bounded
findings.detail: metadata.spec_id is writable tracker data. R1/R3 keep it out of selectable membership, using it only for near-miss reporting and as an additional positive MF-3 dependency-membership disjunct. Plan-form identity, the unchanged lineage resolver and plan mapping still bound selection; R1.8 checks lineage/spec agreement and dispatches into that lineage spec. R6's evidence hash binds bytes, not truth or human approval, and the marker is explicitly unauthenticated. Nevertheless an old marker never authorizes a claim: each override claim needs a fresh scoped flag and evidence. Dispatch coverage is a subset test over the current signal's complete canonical failure-record digests; added failures uncover, removed failures stay covered, and an indeterminate record cannot be overridden. The round-6 mapping-source change can produce a selection/readiness disagreement between checkouts, but the divergence is now named and readiness still evaluates before claim mutation. I established no additional fail-open from that change.

findings.title: F5 implementation must inspect errors before bead filtering
findings.detail: Implementation caution, not an unmet specification requirement: internal/panel/panel.go:269 ForBead deliberately drops registrations with Err != nil; Scan returns a parse-error registration in its unfiltered result, and its globbing is forgiving. In the scratch fixture, an invalid panel.json produces two Scan registrations but only one ForBead registration. A literal loop over ForBead alone would therefore lose a panel read/parse error. R4.2(F5), spec.md:428, already requires those errors to refuse, so implementation must preserve that requirement before filtering, and must not describe the existing best-effort scanner as intrinsically fail-closed. The predicate probe explicitly checks raw Scan errors first and refuses the malformed JSON. This can be handled caller-side without changing the panel gate's existing trust contract; no specification change is required for this approval.

findings.title: Verification and scope
findings.detail: The source and scratch clone resolve to 8b3a5535fcd7297031d8a434ec7a1f26eee77887. The reviewed round-6 diff changes only spec.md (84 insertions, 39 deletions). TestG2Round6TrustBoundary passed and wrote round6-probe.json. Thirteen existing lifecycle tests passed, covering fake/anonymous/unrecognized nominations, forged or inconsistent bindings, genuine primary-path convergence, surviving-tip contradictions, audited binding repair, true/masked reverts and stale older remerge repair. Both inconsistent-binding subcases also passed. These tests verify existing primitives, not the unimplemented spec-129 features. go run ./cmd/mindspec validate spec 129-readiness-tracker-honesty exited 0 and reported one warning: lifecycle-binding: spec has no beads epic; run spec approve to create one. The suggested mutation was not run. All writes, build/test temporary files and probes were confined to the authorized scratch directory; the source repository was not modified.

findings.title: Errors in this BRIEF
findings.detail: Two minor scope/instruction inaccuracies, neither affecting this approval. First, round 6's unqualified '59 registrations on main, zero -r* directories' describes the spec-co-located subset, not every tracked panel on main. git ls-tree plus JSON reads at e2325e36, 8b3a5535 and the clone's origin/main find 72 tracked panel.json files in total, 59 under .mindspec/specs, and an existing .mindspec/reviews/prerelease-r2/panel.json outside that subset. That prerelease panel has bead_id null, so it is not an F2 counterexample. registration-count.json records the counts and commits. Second, the generic reviewer-conduct worktree-add example would write linked-worktree administrative records in the supposedly read-only source repository. I followed the user's explicit no-hardlinks clone instruction instead. The verdict destination conflict is expressly resolved by the later override and the user prompt, so it is not an unresolved error. No material round-6 design misstatement was found.
